Author: Translate By Kyaw Kyaw Win
Title: DELTA MATE Myanmar factory cut the wages saying that no enough ordersJan 04, 2024
Content:
By Min Ni Kyaw -Dec 23, 2023

DELTA MATE Myanmar Co., Ltd factory, which manufactures GUESS women's nightgowns, is cutting 20% ​​of workers' wages because of low orders, the workers said.

"They pay like this every year. We have been experiencing this for over 3 years now. The working time is only half a day," said one of the workers.

She said that they can go back from work after working from 7:30 in the morning to 11:30 in the afternoon. But the workers who are far away from the factory have to return with their own plans.

"They don't provide a ferry to those who live far away. They paid 3000. But the workers have to spent 5,000 to get home. As we get paid only 80 percent, leaving only around 2,000 kyats wages are left.” a worker explained.

She said that only 80% of wages are paid from December to the end of April with the reasons of low orders happen every year, so they have to without full wages for about 5 months every year. Even though the full daily wage is paid, the hourly wage is only half, which is about 30 percent less than the regular wage.

"Daily wage is 80 percent and hourly rate is only 50 percent. It is convenient only because of the full daily fee. We only got more than 170,000 in total including the government substidy. Normally, about 220,000kyats. Orders are full," said the workers.

The workers also said that as the factory gave workers' leaders (Leaders) as normal without reducing their benefits, they were discriminated against even though they were the same among the workers inside.

"Workers are not paid overtime, but 46 hours rate for overtime is calculated for leaders. They pay full amount for the leaders such as leader fee and meal fees. In a department of the factory, a Korean instructor let all the workers go but leave the leaders. He do this even if there are jobs to do. Salary is discriminated and also discriminate at work," the workers said.

The workers said they were constantly discriminated against by their Korean supervisors, even though they had to redo the work left unfinished by the leaders in the next day.

"We want to get paid, according to the law. And not to discriminate us. We are having much seniority here. We know who do what," said one of the workers.

DELTA MATE Myanmar Co., Ltd factory is located in Kyar Kyan village, Hleku township, Yangon and it is said that around 1000 workers are working in the factory and. no trade union or WCC is formed.

Author: Translate By Kyaw Kyaw Win
Title: RONG DA Garment factory violated the instruction to force to work more than 30 hours overtimeJan 04, 2024
Content:
By Min Ni Kyaw -Dec 23, 2023

The RONG DA Garment factory is calling for 3 hours of overtime every day and forcing them to work on Sundays, the garment workers said.

The guidelines on the Ministry of Labor website state that overtime work should not exceed 20 hours.

"Overtime at the factory is 3 hours daily from Monday to Friday. On Saturday, it is until 7:00 p.m. We have to work overtime for 7 hours. In November, we have to work 3 days out of 4 off days. In month December we only have 1 day rest. They are telling us to work substitute on Sunday for the Christmas too," said one of the workers.

The Ministry of Labor guidelines state that 3 hours of overtime can be called from Monday to Friday and 5 hours of overtime on Saturdays. In addition, overtime calls must be submitted to relevant labor offices with a letter of the worker's agreement to work overtime.

"There was no advance notice that the factory would call for overtime. There is no asking the consent of the workers. We can’t refuse too. In some departments of the factory, there are people who have to work until 12 midnight. They had to sleep in the factory. Even if we have to work overtime in the evening, they don't give a break. We had to work until 7pm. We can't eat anything or take a rest," a worker said.

A factory worker explained that RONG DA Garment Factory's normal working hours are from 7:30 AM to 4:00 PM but they have to work continuously without a break from 12:00 to 7:00 after the afternoon break.

Myanmar's law on workplaces stipulates that a certain working time period should not exceed 5 hours and that there should be breaks.

“Leaves are not allowed unless you are comfortable with the leaders. It's been a year since I've been working overtime like that. It's been almost 2 months to work on Sundays. I'm tired enough to not want to go to work. What I want is to close days like Sundays and Christmas," said a worker.

At the RONG DA Garment factory, for health and social reasons, the supervisors said that they were angry with the workers who did not work overtime even though they were allowed to take a gate pass after the lunch break.

Author: Translate By Kyaw Kyaw Win
Title: The Arbitration Council decision, which rejected the workers' attorneys, harmed the workersJan 04, 2024
Content:
By Min Ni Kyaw -Dec 21, 2023

One of the aid members said that the two female workers were harmed by the decision of the Yangon regional arbitration board that did not accept the representatives of the two workers who were fired.

"During the inspection, the arbitration board accept the employer’s representative who was not a holder of a lawyer's certificate, neither is the manager nor who have a complete power of attorney. But the arbitration board did not accept the labor side’s official lawyer with a lawyer's license.How can the workers solve this? This is where the jury is biased. I just want to say that they are bullying the workers together with the businessmen," said a member of the support group.

The workshop and labor law inspection team inspected the garment factory of Myanmar Lucky Phoenix International Co., Ltd in No.135 Pyin Si Min Thar Kyi Road,Shwe Pyi Thar Industrial Zone (3) and Ma Saung Thazin telled the truth that they do not receive overtime wages upon inquires of whether they had received overtime pay, the factory fired her in November 19th.

Therefore, the two workers took steps to solve the problem, but because they could not find a solution, they presented it to the jury for a decision.

The employer's representative of the panel said that only authorized lawyers are allowed to participate in the settlement at the Yangon regional arbitration panel, so the two workers' representatives were interrogated one-sidedly without lawyers.

"When the decision was made, the request letter and the testimony of the township mediation team were thrown away and the decision was made to ask only the workers without a worker's representative. What I want to say is whether it is possible to make a fair decision without labor representative lawyers," said a member of the support group.

Although 2 workers asked for "interim compensation and reinstatement", the panel reviewed that the workers without a representative said "they will return to work only after paying interim compensation".

"After deciding, the jury reviewed that the workers will not return to work again if they don't get compensation for the interim period. Then, it is decided that there is no need to pay notice fee and interim damages for 2 workers including Daw Saung Thazin. They fired them for telling the truth about overtime wages. The problem is the factory’s problem. But the workers were fired and their wages suffered. At the tribunal, the representative representing the workers was not accepted and decided that there was no need to pay interim damages. How much do the workers suffer? Just think about it," he said.

As this decision was signed by three government department representatives, three business representatives and two labor representatives in the Yangon regional arbitration panel, labor activists said that the structure of the arbitration panel was also criticize able.

Author: Translate By Kyaw Kyaw Win
Title: Myanmar Guotai Huasheng Glory Fashion Garment Factory workers having difficulties to withdraw the salaries as it is changed to bank card systemDec 28, 2023
Content:
By Hsu Latt Phyu -Dec 20, 2023

At the Myanmar Guotai Huasheng Glory Fashion Garment Factory opened at No. (-), U Htun Nyo Street, Industrial Zone (2), Hlaing Thar Yar Township, Yangon, the workers said that because the payment of workers' wages was changed to a bank card system, they are facing difficulties in withdrawing their wages.

The workers said that the salary was previously paid in cash, but since November, it has been changed to the bank card, which was set unilaterally without asking the workers' consent.

The worker said that they faced difficulties because on the 5th of the new month, the day the salary is issued, they had to pay the expenses immediately.

In addition, it is said that some workers were resigned as they were forced to go back to the home town and register identity cards in order to pay their salaries through the bank card system.

"The salary that we get is to pay for water, electricity, and one month's expenses the day it issued and it is not enough. In this situation, the manager decided to change to the bank card system on his own accord. We need machines to issue our own wages, and we can't issue them everywhere, so we can't use our own money," said the worker who is facing difficulties.

"As for the workers who were asked register identity cards, they were not asked to go with casual leave and seniority leave. The time takes about a week, and they were reduced to 5,800 kyats of daily wages, 20,000 kyats of attendance bonus, and professional fees and bonuses. The worker who has to go back is not comfortable considering the cut and cost to make identity. This one sided decision make us suffer and the money also can’t be withdrawn all,” said a worker.

In addition, 40 fabrics are asked for a record hourly rate which is more than the workers can handle in the workplace. The worker said that over 700 workers are sewing branded clothes such as Inextenso and CORTEFIEL.

"The records requested by the employer it's hard to meet the standards they ask for if it is a soft fabric. We don't drink water, don't go to the toilet during working hours, and work hard to meet the targets. When asking for the records, the line super, especially the Line 14 and Line 16 Supers, scream and shout every day from the top of the line," the worker said.

She said that workers are discriminated against in the workplace, and managers and security personnel search for workers' belongings after meals and when they go to the toilet.

"While we are eating and going to toilet, and if there is no one there, the manager and the security search our belongings. Every morning, the security checks at the entrance of the factory. Although we told them not to search when there's no one. The manager replied as ‘I will do as I like, and I'll check when I want to in my factory.’ Workers who have been members of the union in the past are also treated with malice by the super supers without fault and the manager don’t take any action although reported. They are doing as they like,” said the worker.

It is reported that the workplace is owned by a Chinese national and there is no organized labor union in the workplace.

The workers said that they want to request not to discriminate against them, supers and all supers not to use slanders and yell while asking for fabric targets, the manager not to search their belongings without noticing them in advance, not to ask targets beyond the limit a worker can sew and to pay the salary with cash for those who are not convenient to withdraw money.

Author: Translate By Kyaw Kyaw Win
Title: Sunrise Myanmar Fashion Garment workers reported about the factory violating the law in the workplace by calling in excessive hoursDec 28, 2023
Content:
By Hsu Latt Phyu -Dec 19, 2023

At Sunrise Myanmar Fashion Garment, which operates with more than 1,000 workers, workers say that the factory is calling excessive overtimes and they face discrimination if they refuse to work overtime.

The worker said that it is difficult because they have to work 2 hours overtime in the regular working hours from 8:00 a.m. to 7:00 p.m., and in these months they have to work overtime until 9:00 p.m. or 12:00 p.m without asking their desires.

"They scold me if I don’t work overtime because of family issue. I'm told that I won't be called the next day as others, and I'm not only called until 12:00 p.m., but on Sunday, when I have to take a day off, I'm called for more time and if I refuse, I'm discriminated against," said the worker, who did not want to be named.

The factory is located at 4 Kyauk Sein Road, Thar Dhu Kan Industrial Zone, Shwe Pyi Thar Township, Yangon Region, and is owned by a Chinese national.

It is reported that there is no labor union in the workplace, and there is no workplace coordination committee. The workers also said that the safety and health measures in the current workplace are weak and there is no solution, and the officials do not negotiate with the workers regarding the violations of the labor law.

It is also known that the factory is manufacturing international brands such as GLOBAL WORK, WOLLYTEC, CINEMA CLUB, HARE, LEPSIL,URBAL FUNCTION , SINCE 1930 UNITED ATHLA, FINO-OUT, LOWRYS FARM, AIRTHERMAL, wmb,CLOSSHI Biz, HK WORKS LONDON and SOLOTEX.

In the workplace, fabric records are being asked for more than they can sew, and although they are constantly sewing to meet the standards they set. Their bonuses are cut for various reasons, and if the fabric records are not met, next month's bonus is also cut, said by a worker who is unsatisfied to the leaders’ mistreatments.

The rights of day laborers in the workplace are also being violated, and a day laborer only gets 4,800 kyats per day and overtime pay, and the same goes for weekends. He said that day laborers are not entitled to the 1,000 kyats stipule raised by the Ministry of Labor.

“I would also like to speak for the day laborers. Day laborers have no rights. They work for only 4,800 a day. They are fired without any compensation if there are few tasks and if they don’t like them anymore" said one worker.

"I have to work overtime every day, and can't take day off even for health and family issues, etc. I want to ask for all of these things, but due to the current political situation, I'm not allowed to, so I reported to the labor office. The officialscame to the office and met with the employer and then went back. Nothing has changed but we are working overtime until 00:00,” said a worker.

They also said that they are not allowed to enjoy leave. They need to have the signatures of 4 people, to take a leave, so they are facing difficulties. And missing a day cause discriminations and warning. Only supers can enjoy leaves but not the other workers.

The workers said that they want to request to ask their desires upon calling overtime and let the workers who don’t want to work leave, not to reduce grade bonus and to provide ferries for those who work overtime.

Furthermore, they said that they also want to request the officials to ask only the possible fabric targets, not to reduce fabric bonus, to settle negotiations, to allow leave with only the signatures of 2 people, not to reduce grade bonus for taking leave, not to yell in the workplace, to appoint the day laborers as permanent, to give equal rights to all workers and not to discriminate.

Author: Translate By Kyaw Kyaw Win
Title: Demotion of a worker cause 29 workers including Super to resign at Li Da Garment Co.,Ltd factoryDec 28, 2023
Content:
By Min Ni Kyaw -Dec 18, 2023

Sources close to the workers say that 29 workers have resigned from the Li Da Garment Co., Ltd. factory, where they demote a super (supervisor) to leader position due to an absent. "When the workers complained to the labor coordination office, the office resolved it in one day. The factory side apologized for everything. They said to go back to work. The workers said that they were not comfortable to continue to work and they did not return to work and asked for compensation. On that same day, the factory gave the compensation at once. It's like everyone has left their jobs," said a person close to the workers.

Solidarity of Trade Union Myanmar has written on its social media that the officials of Li Da Garment Co.,Ltd. forced the workers to work overtime all light and all night. There are also layoffs and benefits such as medical and casual leaves are not allowed. The factory opened on June 1, and the workers said that they have been paying social security fees every month. However, they complain as the factory side fail to give.

One of the workers said that due to the demotion of the line leader, super, and the statement that the line workers would be moved and replaced with other workers, negotiations had been going on for the whole day, but they had not been resolved, so they filed a complaint with the labor office.

“The HR department dragged out the super from the workplace machine line. Its disfigured. The line workers were traumatized when others were called to the machine line. The person in charge of the factory spoke to resign together with the leader," she said.

The Li Da Garment Co., Ltd factory has around 250 employees. There are no nurses, medic-clinic and medical supplies. In addition, the workers said that there are only 3 toilets that employees can use in the workplace.

"We didn't leave according to our desire, It is not easy to find a job now. We will have to complete the cases that we reported. There are almost 30 workers, so we will try to find jobs again," said one of the workers.

Li Da Garment Co., Ltd. factory is a Chinese national-owned factory, located at No. (159), Utthaphaya Road, Thar Du Kan Industrial Zone. The workers said that it is a factory that manufacture brand fabrics through intermediary, and there are no trade unions in the workplace, nor has the WCC been formed.

Author: Translate By Kyaw Kyaw Win
Title: Myanmar BAGO NTMODE Garment factory hired child laborers and breaking the law by not signing an EC contractDec 26, 2023
Content:
By Min Ni Kyaw -Dec 17, 2023

Bagu-based Myanmar BAGO NTMODE Garment Co., Ltd factory employs many child laborers and violates the law by not signing an EC contract on the employment of other workers, the factory workers said.

"Currently, there are around 600 factory workers. Around 100 are day laborers. Most of them are child workers. Most of them works in machine lines. Some have been working around for years. Some seven or eight months. All are young children. They are not appointed as permeant. They are just hired as day laborers for the day," the factory workers said.

Those underage child laborers have to work on par with other workers and receive 4,800 kyats per day and 1,200 for overtime.

One of the day laborers said that they do not get the professional fee, attendance bonus and the subsidy issued by the ministry, but only get their wages on the 5th day after the end of the month. In addition, all workers, including day laborers working at the factory, are not entitled to benefits.

“Day workers are not allowed to come to work if there is inspection the factory. No wages for those days too. Factory workers don't know about casual leave. Because the factory does not allow it. They only know about medical leave. They have to sign warning for taking 2 days continuously. There is no service leave and also no money equivalent for that. A worker with much cancelled fabrics cut from overtime wages. The factory do not give and its like compensation,” they said.

The Myanmar BAGO NTMODE Garment Co., Ltd factory did not inform the workers of the overtime and did not arrange a transportation vehicle in advance, violating the EC contract, the workers said.

One of the workers said that there is discrimination among the factory workers as the bonus is given only to the sewing workers in the factory and not to other departments.

"We have to work two hours overtime every day. There is no advance notice and signing. There are only two ferries to Thanat Pin. The workers from Bagu have to come with their own plans. We only got more than 200,000 kyats for working the whole month.We can’t save anything for food. The bonus fee is entitled to only one machine line. The rest of the departments are not. Although if the factory is the same, the income is different. This is the only factory that have these issues in Bago. Even if other factories pay 15,000 for attendance bonus, this factory only pays 12,000.” said a worker.

Pregnant workers are also forced the same with other workers without being asked to work light tasks separately workers say that the supervisors in the factory swear rudely, and the working conditions are also bad.

“Factory toilets are also unsafe. It's very low and not convenient. For drinking water, there is only one cup in one place. The clinic is a small room and it is always closed. We had to buy medicine from outside. Swearing by supervisors is enormous. I don’t know how the victims would feel but even the passive witnessers are embarrassed. We don't even know what the WCC is. We are going to be got layoff if we report, there was a case a worker got fired because she told the truth to the inspectors," one worker said.

The workers said that the factory's clinic is always closed without medicine and is only pretended to be opened when there are inspectors, and as the WCC team is just a show off, they are unable to complain about labor rights violations.

Myanmar BAGO NTMODE Garment Co., Ltd factory is owned by a Chinese national and operating in Mar Ga Street, Bo Kone 18 Ward, Hinthar Kone, Thanat Pin Road, Bago.

Author: Translate By Kyaw Kyaw Win
Title: HONE KONG ENTERPRIST vermicelli factory workers request to give them the benefits that are legal labor rightsDec 26, 2023
Content:
By Hsu Latt Phyu -Dec 16, 2023

More than 100 workers at the HONE KONG ENTERPRIST vermicelli factory are working without benefits and the workers said that they want to ask for safety measures and health measures to be implemented.

The factory, which was opened on MinDhtathi Kyawswar Road, Township Industrial Zone 1, Hlaing Thar Yar is owned by Burmese national, and the workers say that they are facing difficulties because they do not have rights under the labor law.

It is reported that there is no trade union to deal with matters related to the employer and worker in the workplace, and there is no workplace coordination committee WCC.

"We don’t get casual leave, medical leave that every worker is entitled to. 4,800 kyats of daily wages and 10,000 kyats of attendance bonus are cut for taking a leave for sick. As there is no overtime, it is a huge loss for us even if we miss one day," the worker said.

Although workers have to pay social security contributions every month, they are not entitled to benefits such as medical leave and do not get a social security card. The worker, who had two fingers amputated due to an occupational injury last October, said he did not receive these social security benefits.

"The employer is not even willing to take responsibility for a worker who got an accident with a machine while working and had two fingers amputated. The worker is not entitled to the benefits of social security contributions. Although the worker refuses to go back to work as he was not fully recovered, we all know that he was forced to go back to work," said a worker from the workplace.

The workers said that the benefits of the labor law, which every worker is entitled to, are being violated. They also said that even though they are forcing children under the age of 18 to work, they hide them when the inspection comes and don’t take responsibilities

The workers from the vermicelli factory said that they want the employer to provide workers with the right to leave and social security benefits, to take responsible for any harm caused while working in the workplace, to provide a convenient dinning place, clean toilets and ferries.

Author: Translate By Kyaw Kyaw Win
Title: Some garment factories closed due to lack of fuel, workers have to work substituteDec 26, 2023
Content:
By Min Ni Kyaw -Dec 16, 2023

In Yangon's industrial zones, some garment factories have been closed due to power cuts and fuel shortages, workers said. The official also said that it is not easy to operate the factory due to the current difficulty in using fuel, and there are also problems between the workers and the factory officials.

"There is no electricity during the factory operating time. Also, in the afternoon and before we leaves. We got electricity for 4 hours in 8 hours. Sometimes it lasts up to 6 hours. I had to talk to the workers. The workers also refused to word substitute as it becomes frequent. They don’t wrong too,” said the administrative official of the garment factory.

The factory management official said that currently, there is no electricity from around 6 to 10 in the morning and from 1 to 3 in the afternoon in the industrial zones. Power cuts in industrial zones have increased this month, forcing them to work longer hours, workers said

"We just sit down as there is no electricity. We work when we got the power back. We can’t go back after the working hours as we have to work while there is electricity. It isn’t overtime. They said it was for the times of electricity shortage. Sometimes I work for it. If it's usually occurring, it's not convenient anymore," said a young female garment worker.

The workers said that the factory was closed for at least one to three days because they could not buy fuel, and the factory official told them to work on Sundays as substitute for those days off. "The factory was closed for 3 days as they couldn't get generator oil. They are telling me to work substitute. The workers were told that they could not work I don't know how they will react. I don't know if the wages will be cut. We come to work on working hours. It's not convenient as it costs more to work a substitute on the weekend," said the workers.

There are some workers who come to Myanmar Labor News to talk about the fact that the factory asked them to work substitutes weekends for the times of electricity and generator oil shortage and they are not paid wages for that.

Author: Translate By Kyaw Kyaw Win
Title: Labor rights violations at K SENG garment factoryDec 21, 2023
Content:
By Hsu Latt Phyu -Dec 15, 2023

At the K SENG Garment Factory, which was opened in Tha Dhu Kan Industrial Zone, Shwe Pyi Thar Township, Yangon Region, international brands such as Beisie / Orsay / CLIQUE are being manufactured and exported with a workforce of about 1,500 workers.

A worker at the factory said that it is a factory owned by Chinese nationals, and the workers are losing their rights because of being called in for excessive overtime, not giving the permission to form a labor union or a workplace coordination committee.

Although the law stipulates that workers’ consent must be asked for overtime in the workplace, the factory is not doing so, forcing, intimidating them, cutting overtime wages, and not giving them the benefits in accordance with the labor law, the dissatisfied worker said.

Workers were forced to work overtime without their will, and have to travel to the work with their own plan as they are not provided a ferry and the factory is pressurizing on the workers who cannot work overtime.

"We don't get legal rights. Only workers who have good relationships with supers and all supers have rights, but the rest don't. This is discrimination. And we are not given social security cards. Pregnant workers and those who take welfare and social security leaves are labeled as absent," said the worker, who did not want to be named.

In the factory where more than 1,500 workers are working, they have to drink the piped water as there is no provident for drinking water, and when the workplace inspections come, the factory officials buy bottles of water and display it to lie them.

In addition, toilets, which are matters of health, is not properly kept according to the number of workers. The worker have to work in hot and humid conditions as there is no air conditioners installed and an imbalance temperature affects their health.

According to the workers, they want the factory officials to resolve the issues such as not permitting to form WCC, a workplace coordination committee that helps improve employer-employee relations in the workplace, calling all night and all light overtime without workers’ consents, cutting overtime wages, not allowing them to enjoy legal benefits, not providing purified water, not providing sufficient medicines in the medic-clinic, not arranging temperature balance within the workplace, not providing clean and sufficient toilets and the ferries the factory provide not having sufficient place for the workers and all supers and supers discriminating to the workers who ask to take leave and when they don’t meet the fabric records.

Author: Translate By Kyaw Kyaw Win
Title: Low income for workers due to reduced fabric feeDec 19, 2023
Content:
By Min Ni Kyaw -Dec 15, 2023

Garment workers in the industrial zone said that their income become low due to the reduction of the set sewing fee (ticket fee).

A machine line supervisor said that some of the garment factories in the country have reduced the wages to one-third, so the workers' income become low.

"Before the coup, they paid 2,400 kyats as sewing fees per garment, But only 750 kyats now. We only got a third. It had to be divided between 40 workers on the machine line. It’s a very low cost. The salary is also low. It's about the same as other wage workers." He said.

In addition, if there are many orders, the factory often reduces the sewing fee.

She continued to say that during the rule of the civilian government, the wages of sewing a garment went from a t minimum of 2,200 kyats to a maximum of 3,200 kyats.

The minimum wage in the country is set at 4,800 Kyats per day, and the income of a garment worker is just over 200,000 Kyats, including overtime wages and increased allowances.

"Some facroties that use ticket system do not pay wages for the weekend. They pay only for 26 days. Most of them pay a reduced fee. From the ticket fee, daily wages and overtime wages are already deducted. Some factories do not deduct but raise the fabric standard and reduced the fee per fabric. So, the wages becomes low and the workers earn less," said the supervisor.

Most of the workers said that the garment fee system is different from ordinary garment workers, and they are working under the pressure of hourly demands. Due to the reduction of the ticket fee, workers said that they are only focusing to complete daily tasks and to sew the number of clothes demanded.

"As the sewing cost is low, we have to sew to meet the standards requested by the factory. It would be paid equally only if we meet those. We can pay living expenses for a month only if we have income. Low income means many difficulties and tiring. To solve these, the wages of clothing and overtime should be raised. It's to set a standard for fair clothing," she said.

Currently, the minimum wage set by Myanmar is very different compared to neighboring countries, and workers' wages are also enormously low, according to labor activists.

Author: Translate By Kyaw Kyaw Win
Title: Organizations on migrant workers urged to cancel the mandatory transfer of 25 percent of basic wagesDec 19, 2023
Content:
By Hsu Latt Phyu -Dec 15, 2023

The network of civil society organizations and labor organizations on Myanmar migrant workers has urged for the rights of migrant workers, including the cancellation of the Military Council's decree that 25% of the basic wages of foreign migrant workers must be returned to their families.

In the announcement of the International Migrant Workers' Day, which falls on December 18th, officials in the country of origin and the country of destination concerned about the rights of migrant workers in Myanmar. It includes 9 points of advice to employers and recruitment agencies.

"There are 9 main demands, the most important of which is that migrant workers must return 25% of their basic salary to their families. Migrant workers have the right to manage their own salary and income. It is a basic right of migrant workers that whether they would transfer 25% of their income or not to their families. It's interpreting their management rights, so we're appealing for that to be canceled," said an official of the network.

Other requests such as to protect violations and exploitation against migrant workers, especially women, face violent exploitation, to protect people from being trafficked, to reduce inequalities, achieve full labor rights standards, to facilitate legal migration channels for domestic workers, to provide the necessary support for the safe return of women migrant workers who are suffering in foreign countries due to illegal brokers and to take effective action against brokers and agencies who violate ethics and laws in accordance with the law are also appealed.

"Nowadays, people are migrating not as domestic workers, but because of the situation in their own country, people choose to migrate. Women go to work as domestic workers, although it is not banned anymore, but because they do not do it in the process of getting an MOU, the women who migrate, mainly in the Middle East, suffer a lot. It's women who are suffering, and that's why, to be honest, the legal way to send them has to be done so that they can go to work safely with evidence," said the official.

Currently, due to the various conditions in Myanmar, more and more workers are migrating to work abroad, and there are many people who are suffering abroad due to the lack of legal protections.

Therefore, to enact laws and protect marine time ​​workers and domestic workers to enjoy the same labor rights as other workers, to provide compensation for damages and other necessary services for migrant workers who become disabled due to various reasons are also included in the statement.

The network of civil society organizations and labor organizations on Myanmar migrant workers issued that migrant workers are important workers for socio-economic development and to overcome the main challenges such as lack of employment opportunities; unemployment, Lack of skill development opportunities, weak education system, differences in language and culture, they are trying to increase opportunities for migrant workers, such as education and social protection, skills training programs and safe and healthy social environments whether they are legal or illegal migrants,

Author: Translate By Kyaw Kyaw Win
Title: YOYIKA GARMENT factory pay the day laborers only 3,600 kyats per day while they are working more than 20 hours overtime a weekDec 16, 2023
Content:
By Min Ni Kyaw -Dec 14, 2023

According to the workers, the YOYIKA GARMENT factory, which is manufacturing the Sinsay brand, violates the minimum wage law and recruits so called helpers as day laborers and only pays them 3,600 kyats a day.

"When they were hired, it was told 3,600 kyats per day and 900 kyats for OT. The workers are paid less but they come to work with the hope that they will become permanent after 3 months. But after about a month, they are not called anymore on the grounds of lack of task "said a factory worker.

The worker said that around 700 workers in the factory are working as permanent workers, and around 100 are day laborers. The day laborers on the sewing line have stable employment, but the day laborers in other departments only have to work for a month at most.

"It can be said that cavities department have stable employment. But there is no such thing to become permanent employee surely after completing 3 months of service. Those who are comfortable with the supers become permanent a month and some don’t even after 5 months. Other departments only have to work for a month at most,” said a factory worker.

Day laborers from other departments in YOYIKA GARMENT factory works all light and all night overtime the same with other permanent workers but get paid 900 kyats as overtime pay.

“Both working hours and overtimes are the same. But the day laborers only gets paid 3,600 kyats for daily wages and 900 kyats for OT. The wages for the same workers are being different. As a day laborer, it's a big loss as the job is not a stable one," said one of the day laborers.

Taking leaves are not allowed in the factory and also workers consent is not asked for overtime. There are cases of being robbed as the workers got back late from overtime, said by the workers.

"There are all night and all light overtimes until three months ago. There was no rest day. Until now, those overtime still exists in other departments. We have to work overtime until 8pm every day, which is late and insecure. There are also those who have been robbed. There is no such thing as a safe return home. They give leaves unfairly among the workers too,” A factory worker said.

The YOYIKA GARMENT factory calls 4 hours overtime every day from 4:00 p.m. to 8:00 p.m. In addition to that, they also call overtime until 8:00 p.m. on Saturdays, the workers said that they are working overtime more than 20 hours per week.

The workers also said that there are 11 machine lines in the factory, and some supers of those machine lines swear them. “They swear rudely. We are not happy to work as they didn’t treat us properly but instead swears. We can’t also work with fresh full mind as we got home late," said the factory workers.

Day laborers want job stability and equal pay, while wage workers want non-discrimination and asking of their consent to work overtime.

YOYIKA GARMENT Co.LTD garment factory is a Chinese-owned factory, and known thatthere is no WCC group in the workplace. The factory is located in Mukyo Kyaung intersection, Shwe Lin Ban Industrial Zone, Hlaing Thar Yar Township, Yangon City.

Author: Translate By Kyaw Kyaw Win
Title: Shuangxi Myanmar garment factory forcing excessive overtimes and committing labor rights violationsDec 16, 2023
Content:
By Hsu Latt Phyu -Dec 14, 2023

A Shuangxi Myanmar Garment Factory worker said that they are forced to work overtime even on public holidays and all night overtime every night, and if they refuse, they are intimidated and discriminated against.

The factory is located at Makhayar Prince Street, Industrial Zone 2, Hlaing Thar Yar Township, Yangon Region. It is owned by a Chinese national and operates with more than 600 workers.

It is also known that JAKO brand adult shirt, pants and jackets are being manufactured by the labor rights violating factory.

In addition to forcing excessive overtime, other violations are also being committedsuch as demanding fabric standards much higher than the workers can sew, making it difficult to reach the target and abolishing the machine lines that do not meet the standards, and sending the workers to other machine lines. So, the workers said that they are having anxieties as the factory’s discriminations are making them to want to leave.

“They demand 40 points per hour for a single worker. Point fabrics are not sewed only a piece at once but two. Some fabrics are difficult. They abolish the cavities that didn’t reach the target and send to other lines. But everyday is miserable as the Chinese woman and the supers are keep scolding us also in the new line too,” a worker who don’t wanted to be named explained the working condition.

They also said that the workers are suffering mentally as they are used slanders and slurs against for not hitting the target.

The worker said that there are more than 20 day laborers with more than 3 to 4 months service, and as there are no permanent appointments for them, these workers are losing their leaves, social security benefits, seniorities, and this is also a violation of labor rights.

“There are some supers who treat the workers fairly. If there are such people, the managers and supers fire them without any grounds. So, the rest of the supers also have bad relations. The workplace became worse as they focus on not to be fired. I want to ask the employers that do they really want to be like that,” a senior worker explained about the labor rights violations within the workplace.

Currently, overtime is also called on Sundays, which is government holidays, and all night overtimes on other days too. it is stipulated in the law to call for overtime according to the consent of the workers but they are calling without their consents and discriminating if they refuse.

"On the days when we have to work until 10:00 p.m., we have to sleep at the factory, and get up in the morning to go back. But they don’t provide a ferry. We have to go back on our own, and came back to the factory ourselves. It's really difficult as they are doing whatever they want to do," the worker said

The workers appeals are to stop the labor rights violations, not to call excessive overtime, to ask their consent prior, to provide ferries for the workers who work overtime, the Chinese all super woman and supers not to use slanders in the work place, not to discriminate the workers and not to fire innocent workers.

Author: Translate By Kyaw Kyaw Win
Title: TOE TET GARMENT factory hired child laborers and not pay service compensationDec 16, 2023

Author: Translate By Kyaw Kyaw Win
Title: Tai Hong factory does not allow medical leave and treatment to workers, including pregnant workers.Dec 08, 2023
Content:
By Yoon Satt -Dec 06, 2023

It is said that the officials of the Tai Hong Garment Factory which locates at War Ta Yar industrial Zone, Shwe Pyi Thar Township, Yangon are not allowing medical leaves to pregnant workers and other workers, and are pressuring them to work.

The workers said that Tai Hong factory is a factory owned by a Chinese national, with around 1,000 workers, and manufacture clothes such as EVERLAST, DIEM and FB SISTER. They also said that there is no labor union formed in the factory, and there is no WCC group organized either.

According to the workers, the factory is using slanders on the pregnant, elderly female workers and those who don't work overtime on Sundays, forcing workers to quit their and to to take time off from work and forcing women workers to carry loads that were impossible for them to carry.

"If employees take medical leave, they do not get daily wages and attendance bonus. Pregnant women cannot take medical leave for two or three days. They don’t tell nothing about taking medical leave for a month. But if we continue to take medical leave for the next month, we will be asked to return the papers and report to the office. Those who took those leaves are forbitten from working overtime from a couple weeks to a month. The janitors are from 40 to 60 years old. They don’t get medical leaves too. Even if the doctor provide a prescription, they said they can’t allow. They make us leave a month if we ask to leave. They make sure they don’t give leaves. Also, there are cases about letting the workers who don’t work overtime on Sunday to take time off for a week,” they said.

The workers, who are comfortable with the factory officials missed 4 days of work, but they were not fired and no need to take time off for a week or a month. There is discrimination among the workers.

The workers of Tai Hong Garment Factory need the legal rights of pregnant workers and benefits and leaves for day laborers. They also said that, they want the factory to stop demanding unlimited hourly rates.

"There are cases of being fired for taking more than 3 days of leaves. Pregnant workers are not appointed for easy tasks but asked the same hourly rate with others. They also get sworn and yelled at if they go to the toilet too often, said the factory workers.

It is known that Tai Hong Garment Factory is recruiting young day laborers and not appointing them as permanent employees even they serve more than 6 months. In addition, a day laborer said that even though the day laborers had to work for over 11 hours from 7 am to 6 pm, they only received 4,500 kyats per day.Even though the day laborers were asked to work overtime until 6:00 p.m. on Sundays, they only get paid 4,500 kyats.

The day laborers said they suffer as they could visit the clinic only a day for workplace accident. They have to treat on their own schedule on the next days, and fired after being told to come back only if they got better.

Author: Translate By Kyaw Kyaw Win
Title: Nearly 400 workers at the VHT Garment Factory from Bago are facing difficulties as the factory has been shut down without payingDec 06, 2023
Content:
By Yoon Satt -Dec 03, 2023

The Vht Garment Factory in Bagu has closed due to the lack of raw materials and some workers are on unpaid leave. This was done without the agreement of the workers.

"As the factory did not get raw materials, some departments were shut down. Those departments were closed on unpaid leave. No salary and information in advance. Many workers are also uncomfortable talking to factory leaders. It doesn’t mean that the whole factory is closed. Almost half of the factory is closed. They have to negotiate with the workers if they would close. We have to negotiate how much we will get paid on days off. It was closed without negotiation and payment. There is no advance notice too," said a worker.

The factory has been closed since November 20th, and after exactly 6 days of closure, the factory reopened for one day of work and then closed again for exactly 6 days. So that the workers are working on a 6 day off and one day work pattern.

"Usually, they have to pay, if it is closed on their side. But they don't pay at all for now. It's closed now and said to come 5 days after the end of the month. Once that day's wages is paid, it will be closed again. All of our wages such as daily wages and attendance bonus are stopped. They closed the factory as they couldn't get raw materials, and other factories did pay if they closed like this," the worker said.

It is also known that a complaint will be submitted to the labor office within the next few days in order to negotiate and resolve the injustice being done, and the reason for the complaint is because the WCC group formed by the employers in the factory do not adjust it and only spoke at the employer's discretion.

There are about 1,000 workers in the garment factory, and more than 300 to 400 workers got closed on the grounds of not enough raw materials, and as they are working on a 6 day off and one day work pattern and the six days on unpaid leave, the workers said that there is no way they can handle the living expenses as they would only get about 10 day wages for the whole month.

"We have a chance to go back to work after the 20th of December. They said they would look at the situation. The leaders and supers of the factory also said the same as the officials of the factory. The workers will have a hard time paying for their expenses as the factory only give for the working days in this month. It is not comfortable. No other labor rights are losing. If we only work for 10 days this whole month, the salary is not convenient for the living expenses. The closure is done by their side, so we want the salary. Even if it is not completely, we would like to be adjusted it by 50 percent," they said.

Author: Translate By Kyaw Kyaw Win
Title: Workers' rights are being violated at BOHUA FASHION garment factoryNov 30, 2023
Content:
By Hsu Latt Phyu -Nov 29, 2023

Workers at the BOHUA FASHION garment factory, which sews Sinsay brand women's and children's shirts, told that their rights are being violated by not letting them entitled to benefits, direct ruled by a Chinese woman, forcing overtime unfairly, not paying some of the overtime wages and intimidated while appointing tasks.

The factory, which is owned by a Chinese national, has been opened at Ministry Road, Shwe Lin Ban Industrial Zone, Hlaing Thar Yar. It is operating with more than 200 workers and does not have a labor union.

Day laborers are hired in the factory and they are facing difficulties as they are forced to work all night and all light overtimes, asked to work many workloads if there are works and fired if there are no orders.

The worker said that they are having a hard time as they were asked for 50 garments per hour, and if the standard was not met, they are cursed rudely and said, "Quit if you can’t”.

"If we don't meet the standards they asked for, Chinese woman calls a meeting where she yells at us to throw away the cloths. If the cloths have errors, they only fire the workers. The normal working hours are from 8:00 am to 4:30 pm. They let us go back at 3:30 pm as there were no orders the previous day. After a week when the fabrics are arrived, they asked us to work until 5:30 am, but we didn't get paid,” the worker said.

It is also said that on calling overtime, the workers were forced to work all night without asking their consent and intimidate to fire if they refused.

“Furthermore, we are not allowed to enjoy casual and medical leaves, if we miss a day of work, 5,600 kyats of daily wages, 30,000 kyats of attendance bonus; a total of 35,600 kyats will be deducted. The overtime fee was also reduced from 1,400 to 1,200 kyats. We also want to get it back. As the workers go to ask paracetamol from the office as there is no medic clinic, they said they don’t have anything. Workers have old social security card but as they don’textend those and make news the workers who paid for social security suffers. And the Chinese Woman, Daw Su Su Hlaing from MR, line 3 super and line 5 super always threatens the workers with the military if they asked for something,” said an unsatisfied worker.

The workers want the factory to reform the above violations and want to request not to forced overtime for free, to ask their consents, not to threat with the military, to provide a medic clinic and a nurse and not to intimidate them.

Author: Translate By Kyaw Kyaw Win
Title: 6 Burmese women were sold to Iraq after leaving for Dubai to work as domestic workersNov 30, 2023
Content:
By Yoon Satt -Nov 29, 2023

The6people who were trafficked said that they are facing difficulties because they were sold to Iraq via Dubai after going to work in Dubai.

The6of them were transported and sold to Iraq via Dubai, andasthey had to work in Iraq but did not receive wages, they contacted the Myanmar agent but the agent told them that they would only be sent back to Myanmar if they paid five thousand US dollars in compensation.

“6 of us came from Myanmar to work in Dubai with the contact of agent Daw Za Za Aung from Yangon. When we arrived in Dubai, the agent from Dubai named Ko Htoo Kyaw waited for us at the airport and sent us to an Arabic couple. It's been over three months now and he hasn't said a word to us if we're okay. They’ve cut contact and blocked us on everything. I sent a message to the Myanmar agents but they didn't even look at the message. We were sent to Iraq from Dubai. We have filed a complaint with the Myanmar Anti-Human Trafficking. But nothing is heard. They only feed us one meal per day. We only have to eat just not to die. Please share more after watching our live. Please help the 6 of us. Being with the agent is trouble,” she said.

"When we complain the agent Daw Zaza Aung, she just scold us. In addition, she asked us to return the 5,000 dollars as compensation. We can't compensate without getting a salary. We can only eat sometimes," she said.

It is also said that the 6 workers were hired as day laborers sometimes and that they received 100,000 Burmese kyats equivalent per day, but they only get 20,000, and the agent takes 80,000. They are only fed a meal per day instead of 3.

"We mortgaged our house to come here. The people from this house are helping us. We are being sold to Iraq while we came to work because of livelihood. We also get paid only a third of the 100,000 kyats per day. No matter what boss we work with, they take two-thirds and give us only one-third," she said.

When these workers first left Myanmar, they left to work because they were supposed to get three hundred dollars, but when they arrived at the employer's house, the agent asked for $900, and the employer refuse. The boss explained them by translating to Burmese that they could not negotiate with the Myanmar agent and sent them back to the agent. They only get 20,000 from 100,000 while living with the agent too.

It is also reported that the 6 of them contacted their family members in Myanmar to inform them of the difficulties they were facing, so they contacted the Human Trafficking Prevention and Suppression Police in Myanmar and filed a complaint.

Such processes are faced by the majority of Burmese workers in Dubai. At present, about 60 Burmese workers went to Dubai as they were told they are granted for job and there are many who have not yet got a job and are huddled in the small room of the Burmese agent.

According to their statements, the Myanmar female domestic helper who went to work as domestic workers in Dubai were took to there by saying that they would get a job, but the agent always asked for more than the salary they would receive from their employers. It is also said that as the employers and agents could not negotiate all of the domestic workers who went to Dubai became unemployed and huddled in the small room of the Burmese agent and got fed only a meal per day.

Author: Translate By Kyaw Kyaw Win
Title: TIAN YU shoe factory is calling for overtime makes the worker lacks of day offsNov 30, 2023
Content:
By Yoon Satt -Nov 27, 2023

According to workers at the TIAN YU shoe factory in Monastery Street, Shwe Lin Ban Industrial Zone, Hlaing Thar Yar Township the workers are being unfairly called for overtime even without getting a day off.

"There are about three thousand workers in the two factories. Everything is the same, even the senior workers are under pressure, so no one dares to say anything. We don't get off on holidays. All way. We had to go down until7:30at night. We didn't get a day off in the whole last month.We only had one Sunday off in the last pay week. We have to work every day until 7:30 pm. We can't take a break as we have to work overtime continuously and we don't have a day off. We can take a break if only we have serious health issues and prescription."

In addition, even though they are called for overtime until there is no rest day in the whole month, they are not easily given leave, even if they take leave for health reasons, but only to the point if their health deteriorates and suffer from excruciating pain and have a prescription. It is said that workers want to be able to take a legal day off, and want to be easily given leave if they take medical leave.

"It's not easy to get leave. The Chinese himself told it. Chinese direct rule here. Daily fee is 5800 and overtime fee is 1400. The main thing is that we want to have a day off on every official public holiday. Now, if we have to work on the full moon day, we don't get paid for daily wage but just overtime. We also have to work on the weekend as they called us. We are tired from working continuously every week. They only allow us a leave if only we are unable to stand, sit down, and suffering from health problems in front of them. Mainly, we want to off on day off and want to take leave easily. As per their rough words, it means we can only leave dead but not alive,” she said.

The factory calls for overtime on Saturdays to get a day off on Sundays, but on also on Sundays the workersdo have to work overtime, and on other public holidays too but only overtime fees are calculated and not the daily wages.Only 28 or 29 days of daily wages are calculated on giving salary and the workers have to work overtime regardless of their desire as they hold grudges on those who don’t.

“They told that Sunday will be off after the afternoon if we work on Saturday but in reality they don’t do it. They also told that they will substitute for the Saturday but they don’t. We have to work on full moon day o f Kasone too. Even on the national day, if it is not colliding with Sunday only overtime fee is given. They should give the daily wages too but they don’t. They told that they don’t care about anywhere we report. Those who complain about such cases in the workplace are held grudges and make them feel uncomfortable so that to resign themselves. So, the workers don’t. Those who don’t come to overtime on off days are taken photos and intimidated.

It is also known that the factory is a Chinese-owned factory, with about three thousand workers manufacturing H&M shoes, and the workers are also directly managed by Chinese people. According to the workers, although there is no trade union at the factory, the WCC is formed and there is no coordination for the sake of the workers.

Author: Translate By Kyaw Kyaw Win
Title: Lon John International workers say they are fired and discriminated against if they refuse to work overtime and no leaves are allowedNov 30, 2023
Content:
By Hsu Latt Phyu -Nov 26, 2023

The Lon John International Chinese-owned factory opened in the Mingalardone Township, Yangon Region has about 600 workers and manufacturing Civil engineering uniforms, and the workers say that there are violations of labor rights in the current workplace, and they want to solve it.

The worker said that due to the fact that they do not receive the legal benefits that every worker is entitled to in the workplace, whether it is due to health or an emergency, 40,000 to 50,000 kyats are cut as daily wages, attendance bonus and grade bonuses are cut.

"Missing a day of work due to illness or other emergency reasons is cut 40,000 to 50,000 kyats. Each worker's bonus is different, so the cut is different. There is no trade union to discuss and negotiate for the workers," said the worker.

In the workplace, workers are asking for 100 pieces of cloth per hour, as it is difficult to meet this standard all supers and supers shout and swear and asking for it and the workers have to work without taking a water break or going to toilet. Even if they meet the record, they are appointed other tasks too.

"The employer unfairly demands the standard of clothing. If the standard is not met, we are asked to sign the warning and if it is 3 times we are fired. They call for overtime on Sundays, such as government holidays, and there are workers who do not go to work for various reasons. They are fired. Those who are not fired are not called for OT the other days like a punishment. After that the managers and all supers rudely pointed their fingers towards our face and swear us badly," said a worker who don’t want to be named.

Workers are collected at least 500 kyat and intimidates the workers who refuse to pay saying that they will not collect donations for them if there is a welfare issue in their family, the worker said.

The workers said that since there are more than 600 workers in the workplace, there are not enough seats during the lunch break so some of them have to sit down on the floor to eat, so that they want to make it convenient for them to sit on the floor and eat.

Workers request for resolvents of not allowing leaves, forced appointing, using slanders as they are violations of the law and the officials to solve the money collecting for no reason and if there is a problem within the workplace.

Author: Translate By Kyaw Kyaw Win
Title: CHEUNG HING MYANMAR Woolen factory workers are having a hard time working with a tap systemNov 30, 2023
Content:
By Hsu Latt Phyu -Nov 25, 2023

Workers at the CHEUNG HING MYANMAR woolen factory which located at Nga Moe Yate Road, War Ta Yar Industrial Zone, Shwe Pyi Thar Township are having a hard time because they are forced to work overtime and not paid during the factory's weekends due to the tap system and excessive demands for fabric standards.

"Right now, the factory is paying 7,000 per hour. We don't want that. We want the 5,800 per hour. And 1,400 per hour for OT. Now, they have paid 7,000 per hour and tap system. To be clear, the daily wages of 7,000 and 210,000 per month, and the attendance bonus 15,000, total more than 225,000. We didn't get paid for the garment because we didn’t sew enough for the whole month. Last month, the factory was closed for 4 days. I missed 2 days, so I only got 170,000 for the whole month," explained the worker.

The workers said that they want to receive 5,600 day wages and OT wages according to the law like other factories. The worker said that the daily rate of 7,000 per day started in June 2023, and the working hours of a day are from 8:00 a.m. to 10:00 p.m. (previously 11:00 a.m.) and the worker said that they were working 14 hours a day.

"It is impossible to do it with the fabric fee. If there are no orders or if they close every 2 days or 3 days, we want to get paid the full wages. The commodity price is high, so we want the full wages. The fabric they provide is sometimes easy and sometimes hard. Those who can sew much get as they work but sometimes, we have to work until 10 o'clock at night not even finished," said a long-term skilled worker.

If the workers miss a day of work, they will be cut 7,000 kyats of daily wages and 15,000 of attendance bonus; a total of 22,000.

"Sometimes there are people who have to work until 4:00 p.m. Some until 8:00 p.m. or 10:00 p.m. For workers, if they get overtime, they want to get paid." said the garment worker.

The worker said that the Chinese-owned factory has more than 600 workers and sews brands such as NEXT, CARTH, and CELIO. The worker also said that there is no labor union in the workplace.

The worker said that after the day fee was changed into the tap system basis, and that there were factory days off and they were not paid for those days, so they wanted to be paid.

"They committed violations against the workers. Last month (October) we were closed for 4 days. We did not pay the daily wages. When audit came to check and they asked us to lie by signing that they paid 70 percent of the 4 days that is 14,400 kyats. We did not really get paid," they said.

According to the workers, they want the resolvent of the violations of labor rights by the employer, not to force them, to pay wages for the days the factory was closed last month, and instead of the tap cut system, they want the daily fee and OT fee system.

Author: Translate By Kyaw Kyaw Win
Title: Hiring as day laborers is on the rise in the garment factorNov 30, 2023
Content:
By Yoon Satt -Nov 24, 2023

Due to the economic downturn since the military coup in Myanmar, local jobs are scarce and daily commodity prices are rising. As factory workers began to demand an increase in the minimum wage, the Military Council Labor Ministry increased the subsidy by 1,000 kyats in last October.

The increase has not changed significantly for workers, and because of cost-cutting by employers, workers have been working without other benefits beyond the minimum wage. Currently, in the garment sector, which employs more than 500,000 domestic workers, labor observers and workers say that due to unwillingness to give workers rights, more and more people are being hired as day laborers.

"That’s right, 500 out of 1,000 workers in our factory are day laborers," said a garment worker in Thar Dhu Kan Industrial Zone.

"Some hire day laborers as they don’t want to pay professionality fees or others. For those with less service, it is impossible to complain the employer although they are not satisfied. As there is a shortage of jobs, the workers work as day laborers just to get a job. There are even various types of day laborers. Those who got paid daily, monthly or weekly. Industrial zone workers mostly get paid by day,” said a labor activist.

A day laborer from Hlaing Thar Yar Industrial Zone said that they are losing their rights although they are professionals as most of the factory employers label them as day laborers and pay at the end of the month but not include the wages on public holidays, most factories do not pay for the weekends although the law stipulate, not getting leaves and seniority as the monthly workers and benefits such as attendance bonus and professionality fees as they are appointed as prohibition.

Regarding the increase in the number of day laborers appointed, a local labor activist said, "They hire day laborers so that they can fire whenever they want. Day laborers can be fired today or tomorrow. That's why they hire day workers. Another thing is that when the day laborers who got paid monthly, as they don't know if they will be fired today or tomorrow, so they won't say anything even if their rights are being violated.". Another thing is that even if the day laborer are fired, they only have to pay less severance. If it's a permanent, they have to pay the annual damages and they don’t want to.”

Currently, there are more than 500 garment factories operating nationwide, creating jobs for over 500,000 workers, and the Myanmar Garment Manufacturers Association has announced that it is the sector that can provide the most domestic employment.

At present, about one-third of the workers employed in factories are day laborers, and if any labor problem occurs, there is no resolvent for it and instead if such cases happen, they are fired immediately as they are day laborers.

I support that day laborers who got paid monthly should be entitled to leaves. They do have it. Even though they knew about the issue of not allowing leaves, the workers did not dare to complain There is a difference between day laborers who get paid daily and monthly. Not even on leaves. There are things like that. They look for laborers with few rights. Day laborers who get paid daily can be paid 5,000 or 6,000 kyats daily butthose who got paid monthly will have professional fees. They started to consider about paying monthly as there are bonuses and attendance allowances. As employers, they prefer less paying and more for free.

They save the salary costs. But to prevent such a thing from happening, we are helping the day laborers to get paid for Sundays which they don't get for. Some workers have service of more than six months to a year. When the employers don't pay those workers for Sunday, we ask for it back if the daily laborers haven't really been paid for because they are factories," said a labor activist.

Currently, in 2023, the Myanmar Garment Industry Association has announced that investments have entered the Myanmar garment sector in droves. The labor activist reviewed that the although business sector is reported growing rapidly, the day laborers hiring are on a rise without the desire to give laborers their rights and there is no concern for the improvement of workers' daily lives.

Currently, the workers have been subjected to labor rights violations. It is also reported that there are fewer people speaking out about their rights being violated, such as not getting overtime pay and not getting leaves and even though they have been working as day laborers for more than six months for a year because of the shortage of domestic jobs and the rise in commodity prices.

Author: Translate By Kyaw Kyaw Win
Title: Rainbow factory said they will not pay wages for the off days after firing 7 union leadersNov 30, 2023
Content:
By Min Ni Kyaw -Nov 23, 2023

The workers told Myanmar Labor News that Rainbow Soap Factory will be closed for 10 days after 7 unionleaders were fired and the officials that they will pay the wages only for 5 days off.

"At first, they said they will be closed for the three days. We were told to work half day on Saturday or on Sundays with daily wages for those weekends. At that time, the union leaders did not accept the day off because there was no law stipulated. 5 days after the union leaders were fired, they called a meeting and said that they will pay for 5 days out of 10 days off but not the other five days" said one of the workers.

The workers said that the factory spoke about the holiday on November 21st, and that the wages for the 5 days would be equalized with the leaves or to work substitute days.

In 2019, when the factory union leaders protested about the workers' damages, the issues even reaches to the arbitration council, and as they won, the court instructed the factory side to drop the lawsuit, but the factory continued to sue.

After nearly 5 years of litigation, the union leaders were ordered by the court on November 15th to pay a fine of 15,000 kyats for two cases. The workers said that Rainbow soap factory officials had fired 7 workers who were sued for violating the EC contract.

"They want to fire union leaders for a long time since the 2019 protest. The supervisors of the township labor department themselves negotiated for the union leaders to resign during the trial period, the. They agreed to pay damages," said one of the workers.

10-day closure of the factory can be assumed as a prevention of a protest in the factory over the dismissal of the factory union leaders and forcing to work substitute days are trying to violate the rules, reviewed the factory workers.

"Since the first time they said the factory would be closed for a while, they said it would be closed for about 10 days. They want the factory workers to take days off instead of being closed. The law clearly states that workers are entitled to wages if the factory closes due to lack of tasks. This is planned to break the law by bargaining with the factory workers,” a worker said.

Chapter 2, Article 4 of the Leave and Working Holidays Act currently in use in Myanmar states that the employer must pay wages for the days that they cannot give the workers tasks.

In addition, the Workshops Act stipulates that if a workshop is temporarily closed, it is necessary to notify the Labor Inspection Department.

The workers said that Myanmar Consumer Enterprise factory that produces Rainbow soap oil is in No.129, Dagon Port Seik Kan Zone 1, Yangon and the owner is an Ethnic Chinese who is a Myanmar citizen.

Around 400 workers are working in the factory and they are manufacturing products such as Rainbow soap cream, Butterfly perfume oil, Bubble brand bath soap, Butterfly Laundry Goon Friend, Diaper Rainbow and Liquid Expert brands Dish soaps, various brand Rainbow brands and Rainbow brand powder.

The workers have said that they are breaking the laws by dismissals and negotiations are being carried although the union and WCC have been formed in the factory,.

Title: Workers' rights are violated at the Nexstar garment factoryNov 28, 2023
Content:

It is said that more than 800 workers working at the Nexstar garment factory opened on Glass minister U Nyunt Road, Industrial Zone 1, Hlaing Thar Yar Township, Yangon, are having to without benefits.

At that factory owned by a Chinese national, the worker said that they are making John Baner and Women Secret brands jackets, pants and shirts and they are not having legal leaves, being demanded more than what they can sew, and forced to leave their jobs.

Title: The labor office's settlement of the Nine Tripod Kyotin glass and aluminum installation and trading company's employer-labor dispute is unfair.Nov 28, 2023
Content:
By Hsu Latt Phyu -Nov 16, 2023

The workers of the Nine Tripod Kyotin glass and aluminum installation and trading which resides in U Myae Street Industrial zone (4), Hlaing Thar Yar Township, Yangon said that the resolution by the Labor Office on the dispute between the employer and the laborer was not fair. The workers said that they wanted to get their 3 years of seniority and the additional allowances specified by the Ministry of Labor.

It is reported that the company is owned by a Chinese national and imports aluminum products from China and installs them and sells them in Myanmar.

There are 25 workers, and both the labor union and workplace coordination committee has been formed.

The worker said that since it has been almost 8 years since the workers have not been given seniority leave in the workplace, they asked to be recalculated with a back date, and since the employer did not resolve it, they complained to the Department of Workshop and Labor Inspection.

"What the workers really want is that they want their seniority to be counted for 3 years. But the head office decided to give them only a year and said that they can go to the court and ask for it if they want for 3 years. The workers only get paid for 1 year and instead of 8,000, the employer gave them 4,800 for only 2,022. We’re not satisfied with that, and if the casual leave and seniority is over 16 days, the supervisor advises the employer that the workers calculate with their daily wages and return to the employer," said the worker.

The worker said that workers who miss work without leave will be cut off to the lack of leave benefits in the workplace and they are not satisfied now as they even asked by the employer to refund the money for now.

"As advised by the supervisor's office, the employer is trying to ask refund from the workers who have taken a total of more than 16 days of leave and seniority. The days of absence because of this dispute are also considered as absents. If it is for the workers' benefits, they resolved by even reducing the existing ones," said the unsatisfied worker.

The workers also report more issues to the labor office such as the manager using slanders against them, forces them to work at other departments and other jobs instead of according to the employment contract, and that the employer did not solve the issues, such as calculating an additional allowance of 1,000 kyats.

“ How did the director of the Department of Labor resolve the issue of increasing the additional allowance was he told the employer to standardize with the increase of the allowance from 10,000 to 40,000 in 2020. He instructed the employer to fill the ones who aren’t get full and to split the surplus," the worker explained.

When the workers were not satisfied with this solution, they asked in writing to the director of the labor department, the director said "You can report to anywhere you like, I have 38 years of service and I will get a pension even if I lost my job," he replied by phone.

"The allowance given in 2020 was given with an agreement that all benefits would be terminated after 5 days of absence from work. it is not related to the additional allowance given by the ministry now at all," the worker explained.

As workers, they want to get their seniority leaves fairly and the payment of additional allowances issued by the ministry.

Author: Translate By Kyaw Kyaw Win
Title: Hearing begins for worker's lawsuit against Pepsi soft drink factory CEO and HR managerNov 21, 2023
Content:
By Yoon Satt -Nov 16, 2023

On November 14, a two-sided interrogation was conducted regarding the lawsuit filed by the worker against the officials of the Pepsi soft drink factory in Mawbe Township according to the Solidarity of Trade Unions Myanmar (STUM), which is supporting the worker’s affair.

"There are objection, defense and orders from both sides of the lawsuit filed against the employer and HR. This is according to civil law case of the law, the question was asked, and the judge made an order weather accept or reject or he also objected. So, the judge has to decree at the next trial," said the person assisting the worker.

The November 15th trial was the 10th trial and the upcoming 11th trial was also rescheduled to the next month, and to decree to the defendant ‘s objection letter on that day.

On July 28th, the employee's lawsuit was heard as the third trial, and the district judge accepted and interrogated the 2 sides of the employer and employee. The entrepreneur delegated an official representative to HR on behalf of the CEO and HR, and the two parties negotiated in the division court according to the legal negotiation procedure.

U Thaung Han, the aggrieved worker who filed the lawsuit, was fired on October 31, 2022 due to his old age in violation of the employment agreement, so he sued for 10,040,000 kyats in legal damages in the Mawbe District Court.

On November 2022, U Thaung Han, who was fired, complained to Labor Guidance office and transferred to the Ttownshipcoordination group. They negotiated 3 times there and accepted the decision of the council, but it was transferred back to Labor Guidance.Labor Guidanceand the Division office collaborated and negotiate three more times to resolve the issue, but there was no resolution, and as the victim worker repeatedly requested the supervisor to issue an order to sue the victim, it was only in mid-March 2023 that the worker was instructed to file a lawsuit.

The worker worked at the Pepsi factory for 20 years and was fired on the 31st day of the 10th month of 2022 in violation of the employment agreement. It is also known that he will receive severance pay of over 5,000,000 kyats according to the seniority.

Author: Translate By Kyaw Kyaw Win
Title: Workers' rights being violated at Myanmar Tiannan garment factoryNov 21, 2023
Content:
By Hsu Latt Phyu -Nov 15, 2023

More than 600 workers are working at the Myanmar Tiannan Garment Factory, which locates in Bandhula Estate, Shwe Pyi Thar Township, and the workers said that the factory are committing violations such as not having the right to benefits in the workplace, not having an EC contract, and being forced directly by Chinese women.

It is reported it is a Chinese owned factory which is manufacturing brands such as FSBN, USA and as BLACK SQUAD and there is no union organized to carry out labor negotiations in the workplace.

The factory manufactures and exports one-set sportswear, and nearly 60 day laborers are hired from 7:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. at a rate of 500 kyats per hour and the same goes to overtime and illegal dismissals are often made.

"The Chinese all super woman unfairly asked the standards such as 50 pieces of cloth per hour, and told us to quit leave if we couldn't meet the standard," said the worker, who did not want to be named.

They have to sew to meet the fabric standards between the working hours of 7:30 a.m. to 4:00 p.m., and workers who do not meet the standard discriminated such as not appointed for overtime and not given a ferry.

Casual leave and medical leave which is the right of workers in the garment industry are not allowed and cut off the money for a leave. The workers said that a day fee (4,800 kyats) and attendance bonus (10,000 Kyats); a total of (14,800 Kyats) are cut for a miss of single day.

"Missing a day due to illness also cost for the daily wage of the Sunday. Also, if they call for overtime on Sunday, we are forced and call without asking our consent. We will be discriminated against if we refuse. And also they ask us to work overtime for free without paying," said the worker, who did not want to be named.

Last February, 2023, after the factory's violations were reported in the media, the labor office found out that child laborers and day laborers were being hired with 500 kyats an hour, so the factory had to pay a fine of 50,000 kyats each, the worker said.

The workers said that they want their legal leaves, the foreigner Chinese woman not to directly manage the workers, to pay for overtime and not to forced by free, to provide clean toilets, a medic-clinic and necessary drugs in the factory.
